transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-04-29
Start time: 15:00 PT
Duration: 54 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Emilia Chen (Redwood SE), Leo Martinez (Redwood CSM), Marta Ruiz (NexCore Head of ML), Daniel Park (NexCore SRE), Alicia Gomez (NexCore VP Product), Tom Nguyen (NexCore Finance)

Auto-summary: Short QBR-style health check. Main asks: keep 99p latency under 350ms on critical route, reduce token spend by 12% via batching/cache, confirm security posture for private deployment.

--- Transcript body ---
[00:00:00] Samir Patel: Hey everyone thanks for carving time, we'll keep this concise. quick agenda — review last quarter usage, call out spikes, cost levers, and agree next steps on the pilot extension.
[00:00:12] Marta Ruiz: Thanks, Samir. morning, yes, we had two big spikes in March tied to feature flag rollout. curious about what you folks saw on caching benefits.
[00:00:28] Emilia Chen: yeah hi Marta — from our side the prefix/KV caching gave a 20-25% token reduction on similar workloads during the internal test, though that's pretty workload dependent. We also had better latency tails when cache hit rate was above 45%.
[00:00:46] Daniel Park: just to add, from infra we saw CPU contention on pod nodes during the spike; not sure if that's batching related or simply more concurrent requests.
[00:00:58] Leo Martinez: and finance flagged the run-rate increase — Tom, you asked us to come prepared with options.
[00:01:06] Tom Nguyen: yeah we want to understand both immediate optimizations and committed capacity tradeoffs — committed monthly vs burst and what SLOs we can guarantee.
[00:01:18] Samir Patel: good, quick framing — Hosted API gives fastest time to value, Dedicated (reserved) gives predictable throughput and lower per-token at steady state. For cost modeling we usually show a three-month run-rate and a committed uplift scenario.
[00:01:34] Alicia Gomez: what's realistic for a 99th percentile SLA on our critical route — currently you're hitting about 420ms right? we need sub-350ms.
[00:01:45] Emilia Chen: yep that's the number we saw in the dashboard. couple levers — bump instance class on the Dedicated pool, reduce max batch window for that route, and increase KV cache TTL for session prefixes. There's also a model quantization profile we can try that reduces latency by ~10% at marginal quality impact.
[00:02:07] Marta Ruiz: model quantization — can we test quality drift, especially on our long-form summarization route?
[00:02:15] Emilia Chen: absolutely, we'll run a controlled eval set. quick note — quantization profiles are model-specific; some architectures degrade more. we can run A/B and surface ROUGE/BLEU-ish metrics or our custom evals.
[00:02:30] Daniel Park: on security, we need to validate KMS integration and audit logs. how mature is the Private deployment option?
[00:02:40] Samir Patel: Private is GA for VPC deployments. we support bring-your-own-KMS and customers can route audit logs to their SIEM. there's an extra workstream for air-gapped on-prem but that's longer lead time.
[00:02:55] Marta Ruiz: do you have a checklist for SOC2 items we can map to our internal audit?
[00:03:02] Leo Martinez: yes, we'll share the SOC2 mapping doc — it includes encryption at rest/transit, SSO/SAML, RBAC controls, certs and audit log retention options.
[00:03:12] Tom Nguyen: retention — how long are inference logs kept in Hosted by default? we need 13 months for compliance.
[00:03:20] Emilia Chen: default is 90 days, but enterprise plans allow extended retention and archiving to your S3 with customer-managed keys. we'll detail costs for archiving.
[00:03:34] Marta Ruiz: back to costs — last quarter tokens spiked 38% month-over-month — are you able to show which routes contributed most?
[00:03:44] Samir Patel: yes we pulled a per-route breakdown — the longform summarization route is about 55% of token spend. the smaller reranking routes are cheap but frequent.
[00:03:56] Alicia Gomez: so we should optimize the summarization pipeline first. what immediate wins do you recommend?
[00:04:04] Emilia Chen: short list — 1) apply prefix caching on repeated user prompts, 2) tune batch sizing per client with dynamic batching disabled on the 99p route, 3) try the 8-bit quantized variant for that model and measure quality.
[00:04:22] Daniel Park: dynamic batching — can that cause tail latency spikes?
[00:04:27] Emilia Chen: it can if the batching waiting window is too long. we can lower the max wait to 15ms for the critical route which reduces batching efficiency but tightens tails.
[00:04:38] Marta Ruiz: what's the predicted token reduction with prefix caching on our workload?
[00:04:42] Samir Patel: based on our tests, if you have many repeated prefixes you'll see 18-27% drop. in your case, we estimate ~12% conservatively because of prefix variety.
[00:04:54] Tom Nguyen: show me pricing scenarios — committed 6-month vs on-demand.
[00:04:58] Samir Patel: we'll send a tailored pricing sheet but quick: committed gets ~22% unit discount plus predictable monthly cap; burst options can be attached for spikes at a higher per-token.
[00:05:12] Alicia Gomez: for the pilot extension, what's the minimal acceptance criteria?
[00:05:17] Leo Martinez: acceptance: 1) 99p latency <350ms for critical route over a 1-week window, 2) token spend reduced by >=10% month-over-month via caching/quantization, 3) SOC2 checklist items acked for next stage.
[00:05:33] Marta Ruiz: ok that seems fair. we'll need a perf window where Redwood runs tests against our staging traf with similar concurrency.
[00:05:41] Emilia Chen: proposed plan: two-week perf window, first week baseline then week two apply config changes. we'll instrument with tracing and share raw traces.
[00:05:52] Daniel Park: we need to be clear about test harness — will Redwood use our staging keys or template keys? can't have prod keys exposed.
[00:05:59] Samir Patel: use staging keys — for Private testing we can deploy a private control plane with customer-managed KMS; for Hosted we can issue scoped test API keys.
[00:06:12] Marta Ruiz: any risk of data leak during these tests?
[00:06:16] Emilia Chen: no PII should be used in the test payloads; we'll redact and follow your data handling guidelines. logs can be disabled or routed to your S3.
[00:06:26] Tom Nguyen: finance wants a cap on pilot spend. can we put a hard cap for the test window?
[00:06:31] Samir Patel: yes we can set quota limits on the account for the duration. we'll include a hard cap in the pilot doc.
[00:06:39] Alicia Gomez: talk me through rollback if quantization causes quality issues in production.
[00:06:45] Emilia Chen: rollbacks are route-level configs — you can pin model versions and auto-fallback to a non-quantized variant on quality regressions. Redwood Optimize also monitors quality and can trigger alerts on regressions for your eval set.
[00:06:59] Marta Ruiz: sweet. any updates on autoscaling and region routing we should consider?
[00:07:05] Samir Patel: yes, Smart routing can send traffic to the nearest region or lower-cost variants if latency stays within thresholds. autoscaler supports min/max pool sizes and warm pools for cold start mitigation.
[00:07:18] Daniel Park: warm pools — what's the cost to keep a warm pool of GPUs per region?
[00:07:23] Samir Patel: varies by instance class; we provided a back-of-envelope in the last deck. we'll include exact numbers in the updated quote.
[00:07:33] Tom Nguyen: anything on billing granularity? hourly vs per-minute?
[00:07:37] Samir Patel: billing is per-second for compute consumption in Dedicated; tokens are billed per 1k tokens with rounding rules, we'll include examples.
[00:07:47] Alicia Gomez: on our roadmap — Q3 we plan to move more of the customer-facing features to the new summarization model. if we do that, what lead time do we need with Redwood?
[00:07:56] Emilia Chen: for model onboarding plus a pilot and QA, typically 4-6 weeks, depends on integration complexity and eval turnaround.
[00:08:06] Marta Ruiz: special ask — can we get a one-pager on model degradation thresholds you use for alerts?
[00:08:12] Leo Martinez: yes we have an ops playbook with thresholds for quality, latency, and error budgets; we'll send that.
[00:08:20] Daniel Park: question on network — is TLS mutual supported on Private?
[00:08:24] Samir Patel: mTLS is supported for Private deployments and we can lock down endpoints to your CIDR ranges.
[00:08:32] Alicia Gomez: ok I want to recap before we run out of time.
[00:08:35] Marta Ruiz: go ahead.
[00:08:36] Alicia Gomez: recap: run perf window in two weeks, apply caching and quantization in week two, target 99p <350ms and token reduction >=10%, share SOC2 mapping and pricing by Samir, set pilot spend cap.
[00:08:49] Samir Patel: that's right — I'll send the quote and pilot doc. Emilia will run the perf plan. Leo will send the SOC2 mapping and ops playbook.
[00:08:59] Leo Martinez: noted.
[00:09:00] Tom Nguyen: one more from finance — can Redwood provide net-new discount if we commit to 12 months after pilot?
[00:09:07] Samir Patel: yes we can structure stepped discounts post-pilot and show modeled savings. we'll propose options.
[00:09:15] Marta Ruiz: sounds good. thanks team.
[00:09:17] Emilia Chen: thanks all, we'll follow up with a calendar invite for the perf window and share test plan.
[00:09:24] Alicia Gomez: appreciate it.
[00:09:28] Samir Patel: thanks, we'll wrap.
